summary: Produced the time-domain ownership decision as ADR 0011 (docs/adr/0011-time-plugin-ownership.md), with the canonical BillableConfirmation (x-owner=time, owned_fact, draft/confirmed/reversed), the frozen time.billable.confirm/v1 command and time.billable_confirmed.v1 event, core.Timesheet/PH-025/PH-217 time facts, the contracts confirmed_time billing template and the settlement/management-revenue boundaries all checked against the shipped code and contracts. The ADR compares option A (new pmo_plugins.time plugin), B (put it in core), C (put it in contracts) and D (defer), with criteria for canonical owner consistency, kernel growth, migration ownership and sequence collisions, manifest/requires fit, routing and command exposure, labor/costing boundaries, test/deploy/rollback cost and future time-domain extraction, and decides option A: a new pmo_plugins.time app as the time write owner, carrying only BillableConfirmation in the first slice. It freezes the 8-field manifest (id=time, requires contracts, capabilities empty), an app-owned migration chain starting at 0001 (no changes to core 0009 / contracts 0002 / settlement 0005), delivery/urls root single-write binding, named-service/browser-only exposure of time.billable.confirm/v1 (no PAT/MCP/personal-AI approval/payment), core.Timesheet kept read-only and uncopied, and no revenue/ledger/cash/open-item/contract-template writes. PH-266's spec gained a frozen 'billable confirmation implementation-slice DoR skeleton' (fields/state machine/permissions/idempotency/amount/migration/exact candidate whitelist/counterexamples/concrete acceptance) for the next planning slot to freeze as PH-269+, without registering it ready; PH-154's spec gained an ownership/boundary note; PH-152/153/154 blockers now record the delivered PH-025/PH-217 capabilities and the ADR/implementation-slice dependency, and all three stay proposed. No scaffold, product code, migration or contract-schema change was made.
